incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: synth-checks-eu-west-1 spiking — 5m window: 28 failures (429), 6 failures (5xx). Paging oncall. pd_incident=PDR-8742 :rotating_light:

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Incident PDR-8742 created and escalated to Priya (oncall). Initial trigger: synthetic-canary probe failure rate > threshold.

Priya (oncall): ack — I'm on it. Starting triage. Can someone dump the latest prober logs?

Ash: grabbing logs now. quick tail from prober host: ```
2026-03-15T09:10:11Z prober eu-west-1 GET /health 200
2026-03-15T09:10:14Z prober eu-west-1 GET /infer 429 Too Many Requests
2026-03-15T09:10:20Z prober eu-west-1 GET /infer 429 Too Many Requests
2026-03-15T09:10:30Z prober eu-west-1 GET /infer 502 Bad Gateway
```

Jordan: I see a change pushed at 09:00 that touched WAF/rate-limits for non-prod IP ranges — ops-deploy/2026-03-15-09:00. Might be related.

Priya (oncall): oof. Probefleet source ranges are in the allowlist, but if the WAF rule tightened global rate windows that could return 429. Can we confirm source IPs?

Ash: probe ips: 10.42.8.0/24 and 10.42.9.0/24. I can grep firewall logs. One sec.

Ash: grep shows WAF returned 429 for those srcs repeatedly: ```
2026-03-15T09:10:14Z waf rule=global-rate src=10.42.8.12 action=throttle status=429
2026-03-15T09:10:20Z waf rule=global-rate src=10.42.9.44 action=throttle status=429
```

Priya (oncall): that aligns. Immediate mitigation: widen synth probe bucket so it bypasses the global throttler. I can update the rate-limit policy to add an exception. Anyone have the runbook command?

Ethan: if you can patch the WAF policy, do it. Add tag allow:synth-probes to exception group, then re-evaluate. I'll prepare rollback steps.

Priya (oncall): applying change now: ```
# add probe cidr to exception for global-rate policy
wafctl update-policy global-rate --add-exception "tag:synth-probes" --cidr 10.42.8.0/24 --cidr 10.42.9.0/24
```

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: PDR-8742 acknowledged by Priya (oncall).

Priya (oncall): change applied — waiting for probes to hit. Monitoring metrics. :eyes:

Ash: post-change logs: ```
2026-03-15T09:11:05Z prober eu-west-1 GET /infer 200
2026-03-15T09:11:11Z prober eu-west-1 GET /infer 200
```

Priya (oncall): probes are greening up. Looks like a rate-limit exception fixed it. Will keep monitoring for two windows (10m).

Jordan: FYI, ops-deploy change 09:00 added a tighter global token bucket to cut noisy traffic; it didn't exclude probes. Need follow-up to add explicit exclusion in the template.

Marta: any customer impact known? Can we check frontend and API SLOs?

Ash: platform metrics show no user-facing 5xx spike — internal synthetic-only. No customer errors in the last 15m.

Priya (oncall): note for post-incident: severity = low / internal-only. I'll hand this over to Ethan for postmortem + runbook updates. Ethan, taking handoff in 20m.

Ethan: taking over monitoring and postmortem. I'll open PDR-8742 runbook ticket and assign. Quick notes: root cause = ops-deploy global-rate policy rollout without synth-probe exclusion. Mitigation = add exception for synth CIDRs; long-term = template change + unit test.

Priya (oncall): thanks all — I'll close the page once we've had 10m stable. If anything regresses ping @Ethan.

Ash: adding timeline + commands to the incident ticket. 

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: PDR-8742 resolved by Priya (oncall). Status: resolved (monitoring).

Ethan: creating follow-up ticket: runbook update + ops-deploy template change. Will assign owner and target next patch.

Marta: noting no external impact; will mark customer-facing communication = none required.

Priya (oncall): final: closing thread, will add retrospective note, and update runbook to include explicit firewall/waf exclusions for probe fleets. Thanks :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Thread closed by Priya (oncall).
